name: Jhilinga (Nepalese Rice Fritters)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors
steps: Boil water in a deep pot.

Slowly add the required amount rice flour and food color into the boiling water, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon. It is same as the process of making dhindo but without the ghee. The mixture should have a good balance and consistency of flour and water.
After it is cooked, process the dough through a noodle machine that can make really thin strips.
Shape the dough strips into circles. Set out in the sun for a few days to dry and set.
Once evenly set, deep fry them in vegetable oil.

culture.text: Jhilinga is a traditional Nepalese food specially popular during festivals. Jhilinga is super crunchy, and is favored by people of all age groups. It is closely associated with people of different ethnicity like the Newars, Gurungs, Magars, Brahmins. Popularity of Jhilinga still largely exists in villages and towns of Nepal. The process of making Jhilinga is really simple requiring minimal ingredients. However, a good set of skilled hands is required to craft the pieces into proper circles.
